CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right middle finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
41-year-old female presents with pain at the end of her right middle finger. Patient was rear-ended in a motor vehicle accident approximately 4-5 days ago while stopped at a four-way stop. The other vehicle struck her from behind. Patient reports becoming angry and made a gesture toward the other driver, striking the ceiling of her car with her right middle finger. X-ray reveals a distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. Patient denies other injuries from the accident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation.

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General exam normal other than tenderness over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger. Tenderness elicited with palpation over the fracture site. No tenderness noted distally.

RESULTS
X-ray of right middle finger shows distal phalanx fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. Patient prescribed tramadol 50 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain, dispensed 8 tablets for 2 days. Patient placed in finger splint. Follow-up x-ray in 2 weeks. Tramadol determined to be safe with current digoxin use.
